title: The Fox and the Goat in the Well
text:
A fox fell into a deep well and could not climb out. The walls were steep and smooth, and he was stuck there, with no idea how he would escape.

After a while a thirsty goat came to the edge of the well and looked down. Seeing the fox, he asked if the water was good. The fox hid his trouble and praised the water to the skies: it was the sweetest he had ever tasted, and the goat should come down and try it for himself.

The goat, thinking only of his thirst, jumped straight in and drank. Then the fox told him the truth: they were both trapped. But he had a plan. If the goat stood up with his front feet against the wall and lowered his horns, the fox would climb up his back, get out, and then pull the goat up after him.

The goat agreed. The fox ran up his back, sprang off his horns and was out of the well in a moment. Then he trotted away. When the goat shouted after him about his promise, the fox called back that if the goat had as much sense as he had beard, he would never have gone down without first seeing how to get up again.
lesson: Before you commit to anything, know your exit. And be wary of anyone who urges you into a situation they are desperate to get out of.
